claims.statement: Template-created new codespaces open in the web editor regardless of the generic personal-editor preference; existing instances may reopen in any supported editor. This entry-point exception qualifies DOCS-CODESPACESTRANSITION-001 rather than proving a universally honored default. Supported-editor and reopen details remain in a separate linked article.

The included-usage fragment points to a troubleshooting article for conserving allowed usage. It gives no concrete saving mechanism, current quota, pricing or authority to modify financial settings; the linked article remains separate.

An application can preview in the embedded Simple Browser automatically when the port's onAutoForward is openPreview, or manually through Preview in Editor. Diagnose mismatch by checking the actual application port, creation-time translation of devcontainer port attributes into editor machine settings and possible dotfiles overwrites. The example port/label are illustrative and configuration existence is not runtime success. The source describes inspecting settings, but no private file was read or command executed.

A blank/error embedded preview can be caused by CSP frame-ancestors restrictions; this is a possible cause, not an observed diagnosis. The source offers a local CSP change or opening a regular browser tab. Do not adopt weakening CSP as a general remediation or claim the alternative always works: preserve security policy and verify the actual cause. Linked CSP documentation, dotfiles instructions and screenshot pixels remain separate; no application or CSP changed.

The trusted-repository step offers all versus selected repositories for the shared GPG/Settings Sync list and recommends a selected list. This UI choice is not a repository trust audit or approval to expand trust; preserve recommendation strength and independent feature-switch distinctions from DOCS-CODESPACESTRUSTSYNC-003. The linked security rationale remains separate.
